newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - June 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - June 30.

text.p: This daily press summary was produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents. For further information on these articles or details of BMC's other international press and broadcast services call Simon McMillan on +44 (0)171 256 5130 or e-mail bmc.co@ft.com
-- BA 'WILL FIRE STAFF WHO GO ON STRIKE'

British Airways has said it will fire and sue any of its cabin and ground staff who go on strike. A secret ballot was held among the 8,500 ground staff on Sunday evening, and leaders of the General Workers' Union were confident that industrial action would take place. BA cabin crews have already voted to strike and the results of the ground workers ballot were to be revealed on Monday.
-- UK AND FRANCE WANT TO SHARE EUROTUNNEL PROFITS

In exchange for an extension of the operating licence of Eurotunnel, the British and French governments are demanding a share of its future profits. Eurotunnel chairman Patrick Ponsolle has indicated that the two countries appeared to be ready to agree in principle to allow Eurotunnel to continue operating the facility 'in the days to come'. Ponsolle said he would agree to give the governments a share of profits if shareholders also received 'a decent return' and if no such payments were levied before 2052.
-- VODAFONE INSTALLS BASE AT HEATHROW

Vodafone, the largest UK mobile operator, has taken initiative to provide users with an improved method of using mobile phones indoors, by installing a base station in Heathrow's Terminal Four. The base will allow mobile users to make and receive phone calls inside the building, and other mobile operators such as Cellnet are experimenting for better methods of providing coverage indoors, including in London Underground tunnels and large business buildings.
-- EU CLOSER TO DEAL ON PREDATORY TAX COMPETITION

Pressure is mounting within the EU for a voluntary code of conduct to stop predatory competition among the 15 member states. The agreement being sought would require EU states to end the practice of luring capital investment and jobs from other states through artificially modified corporation tax and other fiscal incentives. Upon its assumption of EU leadership on Monday, Luxembourg has announced it is prepared to make tax reform a priority.
-- SAFEWAY TO START USING RAIL TO SUPPLY STORES

UK supermarket group Safeway will begin trials of a new system of transporting goods between the Midlands and Scotland via rail. A train will carry 'roadrailer' units - specially designed road units minus the cab - hoping to avoid recent problems caused by increasing traffic congestion, including the delay of shipments. English, Welsh & Scottish Railway will
operate trains for the venture.
-- WHITBREAD TO CRACK DOWN ON ALCOPOP SALES

Whitbread, a major manufacturer and retailer of alcopops, has preceded the government in announcing plans to crack down on the sale of the drinks to underage drinkers. Among the methods proposed include the placing of alcopops behind counters in retailers, issuing a rule requiring retailers to check the customers' ID before a purchase is made, increasing the price of alcopops in pubs and changing the packaging of certain flavours so they appeal more to adults than children.
-- ITALY EXPECTS ENI OFFERING TO RAISE 4.78BN STG

The Italian government is believed to have raised up to 4.78 billion stg from the sale of a third tranche of shares in energy and chemicals conglomerate Eni after it was three times subscribed. Italian treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi has said proceeds from the sale, Italy's largest equity offering to date, will cut government shareholding in the utility from 69.1 per cent to 51.5 per cent.
-- GAZPROM KEEPS OUTSIDER OUT

Against the wishes of its minority investors, Russian gas monopoly Gazprom has re-elected Rem Vyakhirev as chairman of the board. The minority investors had pressed for an outside director to the board. In a speech to shareholders, Vyakhirev warned that the company's capital expenditure was 4.3 billion stg less than planned due to the failure of Gazprom's customers to pay their bills, and announced the creation of a separate company, Gazprom Invest Holding, which will help deal with the utility's financial concerns.
-- MOULINEX JUNK BOND BOOSTS EUROPEAN MARKET

French household appliances group Moulinex has launched the first French franc-denominated high-yield bond at FFr300m ($51.54), lifting Europe's struggling junk bond market. It is the fifth bond to be issued since the market opened earlier in the year and is priced to yield an interest rate 2.1 percentage points above Libor. Moulinex is in the process of a sweeping restructuring plan designed to return it to prosperity. For a full range of news monitoring services, phone BMC
